before.name: Question 1
before.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-2y+z=1 \\ 2x-y-z=-1 \\ -2x+4y-2z=-2\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form.

decision.explanation: Apply R2 ← R2 − 2R1 and R3 ← R3 + 2R1. The third row becomes zero and the second becomes [0,3,−3,−3]. Divide R2 by 3, then apply R1 ← R1 + 2R2 to obtain the reduced row echelon form in option a.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-2y+z=1 \\ 2x-y-z=-1 \\ -2x+4y-2z=-2\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form.
after.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & -1 & -1 \\ -2 & 4 & -2 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & -1 & -1 \\ -2 & 4 & -2 & -2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & -3 & -3 \\ -2 & 4 & -2 & -2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & -3 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the $1$st and $2$nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only. This gives,

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

The augmented matrix for this system is M=[1−2112−1−1−1−24−2−2].

Transforming M to reduced row echelon form, we have

M∼[1−2112−1−1−1−24−2−2]R2:=R2−2R1∼[1−21103−3−3−24−2−2]R3:=R3+2R1∼[1−21103−3−30000]R2:=13R2∼[1−21101−1−10000].

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the 1st and 2nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only. This gives,

M∼[1−21101−1−10000]R1:=R1+2R2∼[10−1−101−1−10000].

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Reduced Row Echelon Form of a Singular 3x3 System With Two Pivots
content.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-2y+z=1 \\ 2x-y-z=-1 \\ -2x+4y-2z=-2\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form.
content.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & -1 & -1 \\ -2 & 4 & -2 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & -1 & -1 \\ -2 & 4 & -2 & -2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & -3 & -3 \\ -2 & 4 & -2 & -2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & -3 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the $1$st and $2$nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only. This gives,

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

b

decision.explanation: Apply R1 ← −R1 to obtain [1,1,3,−1]. Then R2 ← R2 − 2R1 and R3 ← R3 + 2R1 make both remaining rows zero. This is reduced row echelon form and matches option e.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-x-y-3z=1 \\ 2x+2y+6z=-2 \\ -2x-2y-6z=2\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form.
after.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 & -3 & 1 \\ 2 & 2 & 6 & -2 \\ -2 & -2 & -6 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 & -3 & 1 \\ 2 & 2 & 6 & -2 \\ -2 & -2 & -6 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=-{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 3 & -1 \\ 2 & 2 & 6 & -2 \\ -2 & -2 & -6 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & -2 & -6 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Reduced Row Echelon Form of a Singular 3x3 System With One Pivot
content.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-x-y-3z=1 \\ 2x+2y+6z=-2 \\ -2x-2y-6z=2\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form.
content.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 & -3 & 1 \\ 2 & 2 & 6 & -2 \\ -2 & -2 & -6 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 & -3 & 1 \\ 2 & 2 & 6 & -2 \\ -2 & -2 & -6 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=-{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 3 & -1 \\ 2 & 2 & 6 & -2 \\ -2 & -2 & -6 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & -2 & -6 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

before.problem:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+2y-2z=1 \\ -3x-6y+6z=-3 \\ 2x+5y=3\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Apply R2 ← R2 + 3R1 and R3 ← R3 − 2R1, then swap R2 and R3. This gives the nonzero rows [1,2,−2,1] and [0,1,4,1]. Applying R1 ← R1 − 2R2 yields RREF rows [1,0,−10,−1], [0,1,4,1], and [0,0,0,0]. Thus x=10z−1 and y=1−4z, with z any real number, matching option a.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+2y-2z=1 \\ -3x-6y+6z=-3 \\ 2x+5y=3\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
after.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -2 & 1 \\ -3 & -6 & 6 & -3 \\ 2 & 5 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Transforming $M$ into reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -2 & 1 \\ -3 & -6 & 6 & -3 \\ 2 & 5 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 5 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the $1$st and $2$nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only. This gives,

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-2){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -10 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-10z=-1 \\ y+4z=1 \\ 0=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any numbers $x,y,z$ form a solution of the final equation, we can remove this equation from the system. 

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $y,$ and we have one free variable, $z.$ That means we need to find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z.$ 

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=10z-1 \\ y=1-4z \\ z=z,\end{aligned}
$$

where $z$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}10z-1 \\ 1-4z \\ z\end{aligned}],\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Reduced Row Echelon Form of a Singular 3x3 System With Two Pivots
content.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+2y-2z=1 \\ -3x-6y+6z=-3 \\ 2x+5y=3\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
content.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -2 & 1 \\ -3 & -6 & 6 & -3 \\ 2 & 5 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Transforming $M$ into reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -2 & 1 \\ -3 & -6 & 6 & -3 \\ 2 & 5 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 5 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the $1$st and $2$nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only. This gives,

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-2){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -10 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-10z=-1 \\ y+4z=1 \\ 0=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any numbers $x,y,z$ form a solution of the final equation, we can remove this equation from the system. 

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $y,$ and we have one free variable, $z.$ That means we need to find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z.$ 

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=10z-1 \\ y=1-4z \\ z=z,\end{aligned}
$$

where $z$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}10z-1 \\ 1-4z \\ z\end{aligned}],\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Swap R1 and R3, then apply R2 ← R2 + R1 and R3 ← R3 − 2R1. The rows become [1,−2,3,−1], [0,1,−1,4], and [0,0,1,−2]. Next apply R2 ← R2 + R3, R1 ← R1 − 3R3, and R1 ← R1 + 2R2. This yields the identity matrix augmented by [9,2,−2], matching option d.

after.name: Question 4
after.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned} & 2x-4y+7z=-4 \\  & -x+3y-4z=5 \\  & x-2y+3z=-1\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Reduced Row Echelon Form of a 3x3 System That Is Not in Row Echelon Form
content.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned} & 2x-4y+7z=-4 \\  & -x+3y-4z=5 \\  & x-2y+3z=-1\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form.

before.name: Question 5
before.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x-3y+z=4 \\  & 3x-8y+5z=10 \\  & -2x+6y-z=-5\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form.

before.html:
Question 5
?

Consider the following system of linear equations: {x−3y+z=43x−8y+5z=10−2x+6y−z=−5 Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to reduced row echelon form.

a
M∼[100230108001−3]
b
M∼[100−23010−80013]
c
M∼[100−23010−40013]
d
M∼[100−25010−4001−3]
e
M∼[100−250108001−3]
Submit

decision.explanation: Apply R2 ← R2 − 3R1 and R3 ← R3 + 2R1 to obtain rows [1,−3,1,4], [0,1,2,−2], and [0,0,1,3]. Then R2 ← R2 − 2R3, R1 ← R1 − R3, and R1 ← R1 + 3R2 give the identity matrix augmented by [−23,−8,3]. Thus option b is the reduced row echelon form.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x-3y+z=4 \\  & 3x-8y+5z=10 \\  & -2x+6y-z=-5\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form.

content.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x-3y+z=4 \\  & 3x-8y+5z=10 \\  & -2x+6y-z=-5\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form.
